1Outcome

Each participant’s right to exercise choice and control over other NDIS support provision is not limited by their choice of specialist disability accommodation dwelling.

2Quality indicators

(1)

Organisational policies are in place that detail how perceived or actual conflicts of interests are managed. The conflict of interest policies are made available to participants in the language, mode of communication and terms which each participant is most likely to understand.

(2)

Conflicts of interest, perceived or actual, are proactively managed and documented.

(3)

The participant is supported to understand the distinction between the provision of specialist disability accommodation and other NDIS supports delivered in the dwelling. Where a specialist disability accommodation provider is delivering both specialist disability accommodation and other NDIS supports to the same participant, there are separate service agreements.

(4)

The participant’s housing rights, including security of tenure, are upheld, irrespective of any decision/s the participant makes about the provision of other NDIS supports within the specialist disability accommodation dwelling (notwithstanding any matters covered by the specialist disability accommodation service agreement).

1Purpose

This policy is the frame for every specialist disability accommodation (SDA) matter at [Provider name]. It names the four thread policies that carry our commitments, and the few rules that bind all of them. It protects the 's rights, their home and their choice of .

2Applies to

  • [Provider name] as a registered NDIS provider of SDA, whether SDA is our only class of supports or one of several.
  • Every we own, lease or manage for SDA, and every dwelling we apply to enrol. This covers every participant who lives in one or is offered a place. A prospective participant has the same rights as a participant (Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 7, clause 1(2)).
  • Everyone who works at or for a dwelling: employees, contractors, tradespeople, agents and volunteers.
  • A participant who provides SDA to themselves. The agreement rule in POL-SDA-03 does not apply to them (SDA Conditions Rule, section 9(3)). The dwelling rules do.
  • Our own supported independent living in an SDA dwelling. POL-SIL-05, POL-SIL-02, POL-SIL-03 and POL-SUP-03 apply as well.
  • Our two roles, as landlord and as support provider to the same participant. Every commitment applies to both.

3Commitments

Each commitment below points to the thread policy that carries it. The thread policy's numbers, roles and records are the only source of truth; this policy restates none of them.

C1

We will do what POL-SDA-02 Rights and Responsibilities Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation) commits to: each participant's rights at home, their privacy, and every request to change their dwelling.

C2

We will do what the provider's Conflict of Interest Policy (POL-GOV-02) commits to, applied to SDA through PRO-SDA-03 Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation): every interest we hold is declared, and a participant's home never depends on their choice of supports.

C3

We will do what POL-SDA-03 Service Agreements with Participants Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation) commits to: a written agreement with every participant, in the terms the law requires.

C4

We will do what POL-SDA-04 Enrolment of SDA Properties Policy commits to: enrolled dwellings kept within their enrolment, lawful, safe and in good repair.

C5

We will do what POL-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Policy (Specialist Disability Accommodation) commits to: fair vacancies, documented arrangements with each SIL provider, and tenancy notices that follow the law.

4Ground rules

The thread policies carry their own ground rules. These four are the ones no thread policy carries, and they bind every SDA procedure.

G1

Every participant has a private bedroom unless they freely choose to share one (SDA Rules 2020, section 24(1)(d)). A participant who chooses to share must tell the in writing, and the NDIA must be satisfied that their needs are not harmed; a notice alone is not the end of it. We help them do it (SDA Rules 2020, section 24(1)(e)).

G2

Where we own or manage the dwelling, we lead on the dwelling, its repairs and its vacancies. A SIL provider leads on the supports it delivers. Where a matter involves both, the arrangement under AGR-SDA-02 SDA and Supported Independent Living Arrangements Agreement names one lead, and both act together.

G3

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole trader names an for concerns in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register, with a written delegation that covers every task the thread policies and procedures give that person. The independent contact is not a relative or business associate of the sole trader, has access to REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register, REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register and the register (REG-GOV-02), and is briefed on PRO-SDA-03 and PRO-SDA-04 Service Agreements with Participants Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) before acting.

G4

If we will miss a time we promised a participant, we tell them before it passes, with the reason and the new date. A time the law sets cannot be moved.

Running every dwelling under POL-SDA-04 and POL-SDA-05. The dwelling records in REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register
Agreements and how they are explained, rent, bond, notices, entries and vacancy consultation under POL-SDA-02, POL-SDA-03 and POL-SDA-05. The tenancy records in REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register

9Words we use

567 words
SDA agreement
the written agreement between us and a participant about their home.
dwelling
a home in which we provide SDA. An enrolled dwelling is one the NDIA has enrolled so that SDA can be provided in it.
participant
a person with disability who lives in a dwelling, or is offered a place in one.
tenant
a person who lives in a dwelling and has a right to be there.
eligible participant
a participant the NDIA has decided is eligible for SDA funding (SDA Rules 2020, section 11).
other supports
every NDIS support a participant gets apart from the home, from us or from anyone else. Examples are SIL, support coordination and plan management.
supported independent living (SIL)
help with, or supervision of, daily tasks so a person can live as independently as possible.
design category and building type
the features the NDIA enrolled a dwelling under. The SDA Rules 2020 set five design categories and four building types.
density limit
a cap on how many eligible participants can be funded for SDA across every dwelling on one parcel of land (SDA Rules 2020, section 31).
conflict of interest
a clash between what we, a worker or someone close to us gains and what is best for the participant. It is actual when it affects a decision, potential when it could, and perceived when it looks as if it could.
security of tenure
a participant's right to keep living in their home unless the SDA agreement and tenancy law allow it to end.
tenancy law
the law of [state or territory] about renting a home, including notices, bonds and entry.
notice to vacate
a written notice that tells a participant they must leave their home.
tenancy action
a notice to vacate, a breach notice, any rent or board increase, a room move, or a change to the agreement or house rules for one participant.
tenure check
the Chief Executive's decision, before a tenancy action is served, on whether anything links it to the participant's support decisions or worries.
modification
a change to the building, or to something fixed to it. An adjustment is a change to how we manage the dwelling, give notice or communicate.
urgent defect
a fault that puts anyone at risk of harm, or stops a participant washing, using the toilet, preparing food, sleeping or leaving home. Examples: no water or power, a gas or electrical fault, a broken lock or door, a failed lift, hoist or fire alarm, a blocked exit.
independent advocate
a person who is not part of [Provider name], chosen by the participant, who speaks up for their wishes and rights. An advocate does not make decisions for them.
independent contact
in a small provider, a person outside our management, named in REG-GOV-01, who acts when the Chief Executive has an interest.
NDIA
the National Disability Insurance Agency. The SDA Rules 2020 give its notices to its CEO.
NDIS Commission
the NDIS Quality and Safeguards Commission.
SDA Manager
the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings.
Tenancy Officer
the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to. In a small provider this is the SDA Manager.
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.
SDA Rules 2020, SDA Conditions Rule, Practice Standards Rules, Complaints Rules, Incident Rules, Quality Indicators
short names for the instruments in Authority.

docs.html:
1Purpose

The result: every in a specialist disability accommodation (SDA) knows, before they choose, what interests we hold. They know their home and their supports are separate. They know their home does not depend on the supports they choose. We record each of these things and keep them true.

This procedure gives effect to the provider's Conflict of Interest Policy (POL-GOV-02) as it applies to SDA, and to POL-SDA-01 Specialist Disability Accommodation Policy, C2.

2When and who

Use this procedure for every participant who lives in, or is offered a place in, a dwelling that [Provider name] enrols or manages as SDA.

These terms are used here:

  • An interest is anything that gives us, a related business, a worker or a worker's relative a gain. It is also anything that gives a reason to prefer one option.
  • A conflict is an interest that affects a decision now (actual) or could affect one later (potential). It is also an interest that could look, to a reasonable person, as if it affects one (perceived). We manage all three.
  • A related business is a business that we, our owners or directors, or a worker's relative own, run or share profit with.
  • A is a , a breach notice, any rent or board increase or a room move. It is also a change to the agreement or house rules for one participant.
  • A is the check at step 23 that a tenancy action does not rest on a support decision or a concern.
  • The is the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. The is the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to; in a small provider this is the SDA Manager.
  • A is a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.
Start atWhen
Step 1A person enquires about a place, or a participant is offered a support from us or a related business. When we adopt this procedure, start here for each current participant within 6 months, beginning with participants who take any support from us or a related business
Step 2Anyone finds an interest that is not in REG-GOV-02 Conflict of Interest Register
Step 17One of the triggers in Decision table 3 happens
Step 18A participant changes, ends or declines a support or a provider
Step 19A provider the participant chose asks to come to the dwelling
Step 22A tenancy action is planned
Step 24A participant says they feel pushed, or you see a link between supports and housing

Who acts:

  • The Tenancy Officer meets participants, explains and records.
  • The SDA Manager owns this procedure, writes our statement of interests, runs the checks and reports.
  • The Chief Executive decides how our interests are managed and decides each tenure check.
  • Every worker, manager and director follows steps 2, 4 and 24. A worker who hears that a participant has changed a support tells the Tenancy Officer the same day.

In a small provider one person may hold several of these roles. A sole trader holds all of them. A sole trader still needs a second person for three things. These are deciding the sole trader's own interests (step 3), the tenure check (step 23) and hearing a concern about the sole trader (step 24). REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register names that person as [independent contact for concerns].

If we also give the participant support coordination or plan management, follow PRO-SCO-01 Support Coordination Conflict of Interest Procedure as well.

3Before you start

  • You can open REG-GOV-02 Conflict of Interest Register and REG-SDA-02 SDA Tenancy and Vacancy Register.
  • You have the participant's FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form.
  • You have STA-GOV-01 Conflict of Interest: Plain Summary in the participant's format.
  • You have AGR-SDA-01 SDA Service Agreement and any support agreement as separate documents.
  • You know the contacts to give: [complaints contact], [independent contact for concerns], [advocacy service] and [tenancy advice service].
  • You know the number, 1800 035 544, and the on-call number: [on-call number].
  • You have read POL-GOV-02 Conflict of Interest Policy and POL-SDA-01 Specialist Disability Accommodation Policy.
  • REG-HRM-02 Training and Competency Register shows you have done the training for this procedure under PRO-HRM-03 Training and Competency Procedure.

4Watch out

  • A home offered on condition of supports. "You can have this room if you use our supports" takes away the participant's choice. It breaks the standard, and the participant may feel unable to say no.
  • A vacancy filled for the support income. A place given for the supports a person will buy, and not for their needs, harms that person and their housemates.
  • A tenancy action after a support choice. A notice, rent change, room move or slow repair soon after a participant changes provider looks like punishment. The participant can lose their home.
  • Telling after the choice. A disclosure made once the participant has decided is too late. They chose without the facts.
  • A signature taken for understanding. A signed record does not show that the participant knows who provides their home and who provides their supports.
  • A worker who steers. A hint, a favour or praise for one provider limits the participant's choice. The participant may not notice it is happening.
  • A provider kept out. Delaying or refusing a provider the participant chose limits their choice. It breaks a condition of our registration.
  • A decision by the person with the interest. A conflict managed by the person who holds it is not managed.

5Steps

Declare and decide

Step 1

The Tenancy Officer

List, on a new FRM-SDA-02, our interests that touch the dwelling and the participant.

Open REG-GOV-02. Read every open row that names this dwelling, a support the participant has or wants, or a worker who supports them. Check that each row has a decision, controls and a review date that has not passed. Write the record numbers on FRM-SDA-02. Write "none" only after you have checked. Give any row that is out of date to the SDA Manager before you go on.

Result
You know which interests must be told, and each has a current decision.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q1 to Q4
Time limit
Before any offer of a place or a support (our standard)

Written on: Form Q1, Form Q2, Form Q3, Form Q4.

Step 2

Any worker, manager or director

If you hold an interest in a support option, the dwelling or its owner, or you find one that is not in REG-GOV-02:

Declare it on FRM-GOV-01.

An interest of a relative or a connected business counts as yours. Complete Sections A and B and give it to the Chief Executive. A manager who finds another person's interest completes it for the organisation. A sole trader gives it to [independent contact for concerns]. Until step 3 is done, take no part in any offer, decision or talk with a participant that the interest touches.

Result
The interest is on record, and the person is out of the matter until it is decided.
Record
FRM-GOV-01 Q4 to Q12
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the interest arising, and always before any decision or talk it touches (our standard)
Step 3

Warning. An interest decided by the person who holds it is not managed, and the participant bears the cost.

The Chief Executive. A sole trader asks [independent contact for concerns].

Decide how each interest of ours that touches an SDA dwelling is managed.

Rate it and set controls with Section C of FRM-GOV-01. For an interest that touches an SDA dwelling, the plan holds the controls in Decision table 1. Write a reason for leaving one out. Give each control an owner and a date. Do not accept a lease or management agreement that ties participants to a support provider. Tell the person the decision in writing.

Result
Each interest has a decision made by someone who does not hold it, with controls, owners and dates.
Record
FRM-GOV-01 Q14 to Q17; REG-GOV-02 (rating, decision, controls)
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the declaration, and before any participant is told (our standard)
Step 4

Every worker, manager and director

Offer or accept no gift, fee, discount or other benefit tied to a participant's choice.

This covers a rent reduction, a free item, a voucher, cash, an upgrade and a payment for a referral. It covers what we give a participant, a family member, a support coordinator or another provider. It also covers what any of them offers us. Refuse the offer and tell the SDA Manager the same day. Integrity, honesty and transparency are a Code of Conduct duty (Code of Conduct Rules, section 6(1)(d)). Declare any other gift on FRM-GOV-01. Never accept money or a loan from a participant. Never borrow from them or sell to them. Never take a place in their will, or act as their attorney, nominee, guardian or administrator. A gift from a participant worth more than the amount the provider's Conflict of Interest Policy (POL-GOV-02) sets ($[set at adoption]) is declared, and the Chief Executive decides what happens to it.

Result
Nobody's choice of home or supports has been bought, and every offer is on record.
Record
FRM-GOV-01 Q11; REG-GOV-02 (gifts and benefits)
Time limit
At the time of the offer. Declare within 5 business days (our standard)

Law changing: from 20 November 2026 section 73VA of the NDIS Act 2013 ("Inducement to provide supports etc. prohibited", inserted by the NDIS Amendment (Securing the NDIS for Future Generations) Act 2026, Schedule 2 Part 8) prohibits inducements to provide supports. This step already applies the ban. The Department publishes 27 November 2026 as the start day; confirm the day when the compilation is published.

Prepare

Step 5

The Tenancy Officer

Find out how the participant wants to be told, and who they want with them.

Read the participant's FRM-RGT-01. Ask again if it is more than 12 months old. Ask who they want at the meeting: an advocate, a family member, a support coordinator or nobody. A person from us or from a related business is never the advocate. Book an interpreter through TIS National on 131 450, or use the National Relay Service, when needed. Check the authority of anyone who decides for the participant. The participant still takes part.

Result
The meeting is set up in the participant's way, with the people they chose.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q5 to Q7
Time limit
Before the meeting, and in time for the policy to reach the participant 3 business days before they are asked to sign (our standard)

Written on: Form Q5, Form Q6, Form Q7.

Step 6

Warning. A statement that leaves out an interest is not a disclosure. The participant then chooses without the facts.

The SDA Manager

Write our statement of interests for this participant.

Use the rows listed at step 1. Cover who owns the dwelling and who is the landlord. Cover every other support we or a related business give or offer, and what we gain either way. Cover any referral arrangement or benefit, and any worker who has declared an interest. Decision table 2 shows what to say in each situation. Write it in plain words, in the participant's format. When we hold no other interest, say so.

Result
The Tenancy Officer has a statement the participant can follow, with nothing left out.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q8 to Q12
Time limit
Before the meeting (our standard)

Written on: Form Q8, Form Q9, Form Q10, Form Q11, Form Q12.

Tell the participant

Step 7

The Tenancy Officer

Give the participant our policy, or explain it.

Give STA-GOV-01 in the format from step 5. Offer POL-GOV-02 in full. Read it aloud if the participant wants. Write the version you used. Do not ask the participant to sign anything yet.

Result
The participant has our policy in a form they can use.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q13
Time limit
At least 3 business days before the participant is asked to sign the SDA service agreement. The participant may ask for less, in their own words. For a current participant, before the review meeting (our standard)

Written on: Form Q13.

Step 8

The Tenancy Officer

Tell the participant about each interest we hold.

Use the statement from step 6, in the participant's own format. Stop after each interest and ask if they have questions. A worker who has declared an interest in this participant's choices takes no part. Write down what you said.

Result
The participant knows every interest we hold before they decide anything.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q14
Time limit
Before the participant makes any choice about their home or supports, and 3 business days before they are asked to sign (our standard)

Written on: Form Q14.

Step 9

The Tenancy Officer

Explain the difference between the home and the supports.

SDA is the home. It does not include the supports given in it (SDA Rules 2020, section 5). Say who provides the home and who provides each support. Say that each has its own agreement and that the participant can change one without the other. Ask the participant to say or show you back three things. Who provides their home? Who provides their supports? What happens to their home if they change a support provider? If they cannot, explain again another way. A signature is not proof of understanding.

Result
The participant can say which is their home and which are their supports.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q15 to Q17
Time limit
At the same meeting as step 8 (our standard)

Written on: Form Q15, Form Q16, Form Q17.

Step 10

The Tenancy Officer

Tell the participant that their home does not depend on the supports they choose.

Say it in plain words. "You keep your home whatever you decide about your supports. Nobody can end your tenancy because of that." Add that the same is true if they complain. Say that neither agreement is a condition of the other. Ask what they heard. Write the words you used and their answer. The duty rests on Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 7, clause 4 and Quality Indicators Guidelines, section 69(4).

Result
The participant knows their home is safe from their support choices.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q18
Time limit
At the same meeting as step 8, and again at each review (our standard)

Written on: Form Q18.

Step 11

The Tenancy Officer

Tell the participant about their choice of provider and the options open to them.

Say they can choose any provider, including none from us, and change at any time. This includes plan management and support coordination. Say how to change: they tell any worker, in any way, and we help with the handover. Say that any provider they choose can come to their home with no fee. Apart from the safety rules every visitor follows, we set no condition on their work. Do not recommend one provider over another. Where we offer a support, also name at least 3 other providers of it in the area, or the NDIS Provider Finder. Use the participant's format. Where fewer than 3 exist, write how many.

Result
The participant knows they can say no to us, and has somewhere to look.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q19 and Q20
Time limit
At the same meeting as step 8 (our standard)

Written on: Form Q19, Form Q20.

Step 12

The Tenancy Officer

Offer the participant independent help and a way to raise a concern.

Offer an , a tenancy advice service and a legal service. None may be run by us or a related business. Write the contacts in the participant's format. Offer to book the first visit, and do not stay in the room unless asked. Give [complaints contact], [independent contact for concerns] and the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. Say that nobody will treat them worse for raising a concern. Someone who holds no interest in the matter manages it.

Result
The participant has an independent route to advice and a way to raise a concern.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q21 and Q22
Time limit
At the same meeting as step 8 (our standard)

Written on: Form Q21, Form Q22.

Step 13

The Tenancy Officer

Record what the participant decided and said.

Write the participant's choice for each support, in their words, with their reasons if they give them. "Not decided" is an answer. Never press for one. Where they chose us, write the date they asked and the date we gave our offer. Write how much time they had and any concern they raised. Follow step 24 for any concern. Ask how they want to acknowledge the record: sign, say it aloud, or decline to sign. Not signing never changes their home or supports.

Result
The participant's own choice and words are on record.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q23 to Q26
Time limit
At the meeting, before you leave or end the call (our standard)

Written on: Form Q23, Form Q24, Form Q25, Form Q26.

Step 14

The Tenancy Officer

Give the participant a copy of the record.

Give it in their format, with the plain summary and the contacts. If no copy is given, write why. File the signed record on the participant's file.

Result
The participant holds what we recorded.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q27
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the meeting (our standard)

Written on: Form Q27.

Agreements and the register

Step 15

Warning. A support term inside the housing agreement can make the home depend on the supports.

The SDA Manager

Check that the agreements are separate and that the offer of the place has no support condition.

Read the SDA service agreement and the offer letter. Read any support agreement we offer: AGR-SUP-01 Service Agreement Template. Each is its own document, with its own signature and date. No term in either makes one depend on the other. The participant can sign the and no support agreement. Remove any linking term before signing. A current participant's signed agreements get the same check. Where another provider gives supported independent living in the dwelling, offer AGR-SDA-02 SDA and Supported Independent Living Arrangements Agreement.

Result
The housing agreement stands alone, whatever supports the participant chooses.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q28 and Q29
Time limit
Before the participant signs, and within 10 business days of the meeting for a current participant. The SDA agreement must be in place before we provide SDA (SDA Conditions Rule, section 9(1); SDA Rules 2020, section 36(1))

Written on: Form Q28, Form Q29.

Step 16

The SDA Manager

Enter the disclosure in REG-GOV-02.

Add the participant's number to the participant field of each row listed at step 1. Add a dated disclosure entry. It holds who told, how, the options offered, what was said about choice and home, the participant's choice and their acknowledgement. Write the record number in the linked-records field. Set the next review date, no more than 12 months away. Link any complaint or other record. Each change is a new version with your name and the reason. For a participant in an SDA dwelling this record replaces Section D of FRM-GOV-01: write its number at Q18 of FRM-GOV-01. The Chief Executive keeps the row.

Result
The register shows each participant told, with a review date.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q37 and Q38; REG-GOV-02 (participant number, disclosure entry, review date, record number)
Time limit
Within 2 business days of the meeting (our standard)

Written on: Form Q37, Form Q38.

Keep it true

Step 17

The SDA Manager

Repeat the disclosure whenever one of the triggers in Decision table 3 happens.

Complete steps 1 to 14 again for each participant affected, with a new FRM-SDA-02. Tell each participant about a change we choose before it takes effect. Their home and their supports stay as they are unless the participant agrees to a change. A current participant gets the same choices as a new one.

Result
Nobody is surprised by a change in who we are or what we sell.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q3
Time limit
Before the change takes effect. For a change we did not choose, within 5 business days of learning of it (our standard)

Written on: Form Q3.

Step 18

The Tenancy Officer

If a participant changes, ends or declines a support or a provider, or says they are thinking of it:

Check that nothing about the participant's home has changed because of it.

Ask the participant in their usual way. Do not rely on records alone. Then check REG-SDA-02 and the dwelling's repairs, rent and notices. Look at the room, keys, visitors and how workers treat the participant. Repairs, notices and visits must be the same for every resident, whatever supports they choose. Ask whether any provider they chose has been refused, delayed or put under a condition. If the participant links a change to their support choice, or you cannot explain it, go to step 25. If a provider was kept out, go to step 20. Check again after 3 months.

Result
A support choice has cost the participant nothing about their home, or the cost is found.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q30 to Q32
Time limit
Within 5 business days of learning of the change, and again 3 months later (our standard)

Written on: Form Q30, Form Q31, Form Q32.

Step 19

The Tenancy Officer

If a provider the participant chose asks to come to the dwelling:

Let the provider in, with no fee and no condition from us.

The participant decides who comes into their home. Give the provider the dwelling's safety information: alarms, exits and the evacuation procedure (AGR-SDA-02 Q27; PRO-SDA-05 step 14). Arrange any building access they need, such as a fob or a code. Do not ask for fees, business terms or a copy of their agreement with the participant. Offer AGR-SDA-02 SDA and Supported Independent Living Arrangements Agreement when the provider gives supported independent living. Deal with a worker who puts anyone in danger under PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure. Do not close the door on the provider.

Result
The provider the participant chose can work in their home.
Record
None
Time limit
Straight away. We never restrict access (SDA Rules 2020, section 37; SDA Conditions Rule, section 10(2)(b))
Step 20

The Chief Executive

If anyone finds that a provider the participant chose was refused, delayed, charged or put under a condition:

Lift the restriction on the provider's access.

Let the provider in the same day. Tell the participant what happened and offer an advocate. Record it as a breach under review: add a row to REG-GOV-02 and set its status to "breach under review". Find out who gave the instruction. The Quality Manager decides whether to tell the NDIS Commission, which can be told at any time on 1800 035 544. Add an improvement to REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register.

Result
The restriction is gone, and its cause is being dealt with.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q32; REG-GOV-02 (status)
Time limit
The same business day (our standard)

Written on: Form Q32.

Step 21

The Tenancy Officer

If a vacancy is being filled, or a place is being offered:

Offer the place with no condition about supports.

Do not ask which provider the person will use. Do not rank people by the supports they will buy. If the person tells you, write nothing that links the offer to it. Decline any request from an owner or a coordinator to prefer people who use a related business. Tell the Chief Executive the same day. Our income from a full dwelling is an interest: it goes in REG-GOV-02 (interest held). PRO-SDA-05 Tenancy Management Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) sets how vacancies are filled.

Result
The offer rests on the person's needs and wishes alone.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q29
Time limit
Before the offer is made (our standard)

Written on: Form Q29.

Step 22

Warning. A notice, rent change, room move or slow repair soon after a support choice can look like punishment. It can be punishment. The participant can lose their home.

The SDA Manager

If a tenancy action is planned for a participant:

Send a tenure check request to the Chief Executive before the action goes out.

Complete Q33 and Q34 of FRM-SDA-02. Write the action and its legal ground in [state or territory tenancy law]. List what the participant has changed, ended, declined or raised in the last 12 months. Use the REG-GOV-02 disclosure entries and REG-FBK-01 Complaints Register. If someone is at immediate risk of harm, act first under PRO-SDA-05 and PRO-INC-01. Then send the request within 2 business days.

Result
No tenancy action goes out unchecked.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q33 and Q34
Time limit
Before the action is served (our standard)

Written on: Form Q33, Form Q34.

Step 23

The Chief Executive. A sole trader, or a Chief Executive who has an interest in the participant's supports, asks [independent contact for concerns].

Decide whether anything links the action to the participant's support decisions or concerns.

Use Decision table 4. Look at the timing and at who asked for the action. Look at the evidence for the ground. Ask whether we would take the same action for another resident. A link counts even when nobody meant it. Write your reasons. If a link is found or cannot be ruled out, the action does not go out.

Result
Each tenancy action stands on its own ground, or stops.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q35 and Q36
Time limit
Within 1 business day of receiving the request, and before the action is served (our standard)

Written on: Form Q35, Form Q36.

Step 24

Any worker

If a participant says or shows they feel pushed or fear for their home, or you see a link between supports and housing:

Tell the SDA Manager what you heard.

If the participant is in distress or at risk of harm, follow WIN-INC-01 Responding to an Incident (frontline) first. Then write the participant's words on FRM-FBK-01. Do not promise an outcome. Do not tell the participant what to choose. Tell them they can phone the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. If the concern is about the SDA Manager or the Chief Executive, tell [independent contact for concerns]. If a notice has already been served, phone the SDA Manager or [on-call number] at once.

Result
The concern is with someone who can act, and the participant knows where else to go.
Record
FRM-FBK-01 Q8 and Q14
Time limit
Before your shift ends. At once if a notice has been served (our standard)

The NDIS Act 2013 protects a person who makes a disclosure that qualifies for protection. It bans victimising that person (NDIS Act 2013, sections 73ZA and 73ZC). POL-GOV-03 Whistleblower and Disclosure Protection Policy sets how we protect you.

Law changing: from 1 July 2027 the disclosure protections in Division 7 of Part 3A of the NDIS Act 2013 are amended, not replaced (new heading "Whistleblower protections", new sections 73ZBAA and 73ZDAA: NDIS Amendment (Securing the NDIS for Future Generations) Act 2026, Schedule 3 Part 4). Sections 73ZA and 73ZC remain, as amended on 9 April 2026 by the NDIS Amendment (Integrity and Safeguarding) Act 2026. Check this step then.

Step 25

The SDA Manager

Hold any tenancy action for the participant.

Serve no tenancy action while the concern is open. The Chief Executive decides the same day whether to withdraw a notice already served, with legal advice if needed. Offer the participant an advocate. Pass the concern to the person who manages complaints under PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure, who holds no interest in the matter. If a breach is suspected, set the row's status to "breach under review" and link the complaint to the row.

Result
The participant is safe at home while the concern is looked into.
Record
REG-GOV-02 (status, linked records)
Time limit
Within 1 business day of the concern reaching you (our standard)
Step 26

The Tenancy Officer

Review the disclosure with each participant every 12 months.

Start a new FRM-SDA-02 at the participant's tenancy review. Look at REG-GOV-02 first, as at step 1. Go through steps 7 to 12 again in their format. Ask whether they want to change any support. Repeat the housing check and the access check at Q31 and Q32 of FRM-SDA-02. Give them a copy. The participant can ask for this review at any time.

Result
The participant's picture of our interests and their rights is current.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q3, Q23 to Q26, Q31, Q32 and Q37
Time limit
Every 12 months from the last review, and when the participant asks (our standard)

Written on: Form Q3, Form Q23, Form Q24, Form Q25, Form Q26, Form Q31, Form Q32, Form Q37.

Step 27

The SDA Manager

Report to the Chief Executive every 3 months on conflicts in SDA dwellings.

Count the disclosures made and the reviews overdue. Count the choices of "us", "another provider" and "none" in the REG-GOV-02 disclosure entries. Count the housing checks and what they found. Count the tenure checks and their outcomes, any refusal or condition on access, and every gift offered. Flag any dwelling where every participant chose our supports. It may be a free choice, but ask. The Chief Executive takes the report and each open row for an interest of ours to the governing body. Add the meeting date and minute reference to each row's governing body review field.

Result
The governing body can see whether choice is real in each dwelling.
Record
REG-GOV-02 (governing body review)
Time limit
Within 10 business days of the end of each 3 months (our standard)
Step 28

The SDA Manager

If an interest of ours ends:

Tell each participant affected that the interest has ended.

Complete a new FRM-SDA-02 saying so, and tell each participant in their format. Then ask the Chief Executive to close the row. Do not close it until every control is done or no longer needed. REG-GOV-02 sets what closed means.

Result
The register shows when an interest ended and that each participant knows.
Record
FRM-SDA-02 Q3; REG-GOV-02 (closed date)
Time limit
Within 5 business days of the interest ending (our standard)

Written on: Form Q3.

6Decision

Decision table 1: the controls for an interest of ours that touches an SDA dwelling (step 3). The plan holds each one unless the decision maker writes a reason.

No.ControlOwnerDone when
1The SDA agreement and any support agreement are separate documents, each signed on its ownSDA ManagerBefore each participant signs (step 15)
2Each offer of a place carries no condition about supportsTenancy OfficerBefore each offer (step 21)
3Each participant hears the disclosure in steps 7 to 14 before they choose, and every 12 monthsTenancy OfficerBefore any choice, then at each review (step 26)
4Any provider the participant chooses can enter, with no fee and no conditionTenancy OfficerEach time a provider asks (step 19)
5A person with no interest in the participant's supports checks each tenancy actionChief ExecutiveBefore each action (steps 22 and 23)
6Independent advice and an independent route for a concern are offeredTenancy OfficerAt each disclosure (step 12)
7Nobody offers or accepts a benefit tied to a choiceEvery workerAt all times (step 4)
8The row is reviewedChief ExecutiveEvery 12 months (REG-GOV-02 review date)

Decision table 2: what the statement says (step 6).

IfThen the statement says
We give SDA and no other support, and hold no other interestThat we give the home only. That we hold no interest in any support the participant chooses. That their home does not depend on their supports
We also give supports in the dwelling, such as supported independent living, support coordination, plan management or therapyThat we give both. That the home and the supports are separate, each with its own agreement. What we earn from each. That the participant can choose another provider for any support
A related business gives supports in the dwellingWho owns it, how we are connected and what each of us gains. That the participant can choose any provider
Another party owns the dwelling and we lease or manage itWho owns it, who the landlord is, and who to ask about repairs and notices. That the owner cannot tie the home to any support
A worker who works with the participant has declared an interestThat a worker has an interest and has stepped aside. Name no one

Decision table 3: when to do the disclosure again, and for whom (step 17).

TriggerWhat to doWhen
A new support starts in the dwelling, or we start a related businessRepeat steps 1 to 14 for every participant in the dwellingBefore it starts
The owner or landlord of the dwelling changesRepeat steps 1 to 14 for every participant in the dwellingBefore the change takes effect
We make a new referral arrangement, or a change in who we are connected toRepeat steps 1 to 14 for every participant it touches. Remember step 4Before it takes effect
12 months since the last recordDo step 26On the review date in REG-GOV-02
We adopt this procedureDo steps 1 to 14 for each current participant, starting with participants who take any support from us or a related businessWithin 6 months of adopting

Decision table 4: the tenure check (step 23). The duty rests on Practice Standards Rules, Schedule 7, clause 4 and Quality Indicators Guidelines, section 69(4); SDA Conditions Rule, section 8(a)(i) supplies the lawful-ground test.

The check findsDecisionWhat happens
The ground is lawful and stands alone. The participant has not changed, ended, declined or raised anything in 12 monthsNo linkThe action goes out. Write the evidence at Q35 of FRM-SDA-02
The participant did change, end, decline or raise something, but the ground is documented and began firstNo linkThe action goes out. Write the dates and the evidence at Q35 of FRM-SDA-02
We would not take the same action for another residentLink not ruled outThe action does not go out. Offer the participant an advocate. Go to step 25
The ground is not lawful in [state or territory tenancy law], or cannot be shownStopThe action does not go out. Find and fix the cause
The participant, an advocate or a worker says the action is linked to a support choiceLink not ruled outThe action does not go out. Go to step 24 and step 25
The Chief Executive has an interest in the participant's supportsNot the Chief Executive's to decide[independent contact for concerns] decides
Someone is at immediate risk of harmAct nowAct under PRO-SDA-05 and PRO-INC-01. Complete the check within 2 business days

7If it goes wrong

IfThen
The participant does not want to talk about thisThat is their right. Do not press. Leave the plain summary and the contacts, in their format. Ask again at another time and place. Write "not discussed" with the date at Q23 of FRM-SDA-02. Do not ask them to sign the SDA agreement until the disclosure has been given and 3 business days have passed
The participant cannot say back what they were told, even with supportAsk again another day, with the person they trust and pictures or objects. Offer an advocate. Use what you know of their will and preferences. Never treat silence as agreement. Write "not yet" at Q17 of FRM-SDA-02 and do not ask them to sign
An interpreter or communication partner cannot be found in timeMove the meeting, not the disclosure. Give the plain summary in the best format you have, and tell the participant the meeting is waiting for the right support. Nobody is asked to sign in the meantime
A guardian or nominee decides for the participantTell both the participant and the decision maker. Write the participant's own view at Q23 of FRM-SDA-02. The participant's home still does not depend on any support choice
A time limit will be missedTell the SDA Manager before it passes. Move the signing date, never the disclosure. Nobody is asked to sign until the time has passed, unless the participant asks for less in their own words at Q24 of FRM-SDA-02. A vacancy or an owner's date is never a reason to shorten it
The Tenancy Officer is awayThe SDA Manager does the steps, or names another trained worker with no interest in the participant's supports. The meeting date moves. The standard does not
A row in REG-GOV-02 is missing, has no decision, or is past its review dateDo step 2 and step 3 first. Do not give the participant a statement that rests on an interest with no decision. Delay the signing, not the facts
You find that a participant chose before they were toldTell the SDA Manager the same day. Tell the participant in full now, and offer to undo any choice at no cost to them. Their home is unaffected. The Chief Executive sets the row's status to "breach under review" and adds an improvement to REG-QMS-01
A participant says they feel pressuredFollow step 24 and step 25
An owner, investor, coordinator or colleague asks for a participant to be steered to a related providerRefuse. Tell the Chief Executive the same day. Declare it under step 2. If the request came from the Chief Executive or a sole trader, tell [independent contact for concerns] or the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544
Your concern is about the SDA Manager or the Chief ExecutiveTell the Chief Executive, or [independent contact for concerns] if the concern is about the Chief Executive or a sole trader. You can phone the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544 at any time. POL-GOV-03 protects you
Fewer than 3 other providers of a support work in the areaWrite how many at Q20 of FRM-SDA-02. Offer visiting or remote providers and the NDIS Provider Finder. Never treat the lack of choice as a reason to make our supports a condition. The participant can choose "none for now"
A current participant has an agreement term that ties their home to supportsTell the Chief Executive the same day. Remove the term in writing with the participant. Offer an advocate. Their home stays. Record it as a breach under review in REG-GOV-02 (status)
The participant wants to move away from our supportsFollow PRO-SUP-04 Transitions to or from a Provider Procedure. Do step 18 within 5 business days
A participant already has a notice and says it is a punishmentGo to step 24 and step 25 the same day. Offer an advocate and the NDIS Commission number
The system is downWrite the record on paper. Enter it within 2 business days of the system coming back

8Done means

For each participant in an SDA dwelling, all of these are true:

  • they heard about each interest we hold before they chose anything, in their own way
  • they can say which is their home and which are their supports
  • the SDA agreement and any support agreement are separate documents, and no term links them
  • they know their home does not depend on their supports, and that any provider they choose may come in
  • they have contacts for independent advice and a way to raise a concern
  • a review date is set within 12 months.

These records now exist:

  • a signed FRM-SDA-02 on the participant's file
  • the participant's number and dated disclosure entries in REG-GOV-02
  • the record number and the review date in REG-GOV-02
  • tenancy entries in REG-SDA-02 where a tenancy action was planned
  • improvements in REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register.

9Quick card

131 words
  • Before any notice, rent change or room move, ask for the tenure check (step 22)
  • If a participant feels pushed, tell the SDA Manager before your shift ends (step 24)
  • Tell the participant about every interest we hold before they choose anything (step 8)
  • Say it plainly: their home does not depend on the supports they choose (step 10)
  • Never make an offer of a place depend on which supports the person will use (step 21)
  • Let in any provider the participant chooses, with no fee or condition (step 19)
  • Keep the SDA agreement and any support agreement as two documents, signed separately (step 15)
  • Offer and accept no gift or benefit tied to a choice (step 4)
  • Repeat the disclosure every 12 months, and whenever our interests change (step 26)

questions.text: Who owns the dwelling, and who is the landlord?
questions.hint: Say if we own it, lease it or manage it for an owner, or if a related business owns it. Say if the owner shares owners, directors or managers with us. Name the owner and the landlord.

options: we own it and are the landlord
we lease it and are the landlord
we manage it for an owner who is the landlord

questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 6.

questions.section: Section C: Our interests (the SDA Manager)
questions.text: Which supports do we, or a related business, give or offer this participant in the dwelling?
questions.hint: Choose every one, even if the participant has already said no. "None" is an answer.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 6.

questions.section: Section C: Our interests (the SDA Manager)
questions.text: What do we, or a related business, gain or lose if the participant chooses our support, and if they choose another?
questions.hint: Use plain words. Include income from supports, payments between related businesses and any gain from a full dwelling.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 6.

questions.section: Section C: Our interests (the SDA Manager)
questions.text: Is there a referral arrangement, fee, commission, gift, discount or other benefit about this participant's choices?
questions.hint: We pay and accept none. "Yes" means stop and tell the Chief Executive the same day.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 6.

questions.section: Section C: Our interests (the SDA Manager)
questions.text: Which workers who talk with this participant about their home or supports have declared an interest?
questions.hint: Write the REG-GOV-02 record numbers of their declarations. A worker with an interest takes no part. Name no worker to the participant.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 6.

questions.section: Section D: Telling the participant (the Tenancy Officer)
questions.text: What did we give or explain about our conflict of interest policy?
questions.hint: Give STA-GOV-01 and offer POL-GOV-02. Write the version you used. Do not ask for a signature yet.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 7.

questions.section: Section D: Telling the participant (the Tenancy Officer)
questions.text: What did we tell the participant about each interest in Section C?
questions.hint: Write the words you used, in the participant's format. Tell them before they choose anything.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 8.

questions.section: Section D: Telling the participant (the Tenancy Officer)
questions.text: Which supports does the participant have or want in this dwelling, and who provides each?
questions.hint: One line each. "Not chosen yet" is an answer. Never ask the participant to choose now.

controls.label: One line each: support; provider (us, a related business, another provider, or not chosen yet); start date

questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 9.

questions.section: Section D: Telling the participant (the Tenancy Officer)
questions.text: What did we say about the difference between the home and the supports?
questions.hint: Cover who provides the home, who provides each support, that each has its own agreement, and that the participant can change one without the other.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 9.

questions.section: Section D: Telling the participant (the Tenancy Officer)
questions.text: What did the participant say or show back?
questions.hint: Ask: who gives you your home? Who gives you your supports? What happens to your home if you change who supports you? A signature is not proof. If the answers are unclear, explain again another way and write that here.

controls.label: The participant's words, signs or pictures

questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 9.

questions.section: Section D: Telling the participant (the Tenancy Officer)
questions.text: Did we tell the participant that their home does not depend on the supports they choose, change or decline?
questions.hint: Say it in plain words. Add that it is also true if they complain, and that neither agreement is a condition of the other.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 10. Recorded in: Register.

questions.section: Section D: Telling the participant (the Tenancy Officer)
questions.text: Did we tell the participant they can choose any provider for any support, including none from us, and change later?
questions.hint: Include plan management and support coordination. Say how to change: they tell any worker, in any way. Say that any provider they choose can come to their home with no fee.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 11.

questions.section: Section D: Telling the participant (the Tenancy Officer)
questions.text: Which other providers, or ways to find one, did we offer?
questions.hint: Where we offer a support, offer at least 3 other providers of it that work in the area, or the NDIS Provider Finder. If fewer than 3 exist, write how many.

controls.label: One line each: provider or finder; date given; format

questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 11.

questions.section: Section D: Telling the participant (the Tenancy Officer)
questions.text: Did we offer independent help, and what did the participant choose?
questions.hint: An <button type="button" class="term" data-term="independent advocate" data-def="a person who is not part of [Provider name], chosen by the participant, who speaks up for their wishes and rights. An advocate does not make decisions for them." data-source="POL-SDA-01">independent advocate</button>, a tenancy advice service or a legal service. None may be run by us or a related business.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 12.

questions.section: Section D: Telling the participant (the Tenancy Officer)
questions.text: Did we tell the participant how to raise a concern, and that it will not affect their home or supports?
questions.hint: Give [complaints contact], [independent contact for concerns] and the on 1800 035 544.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 12.

questions.section: Section E: What the participant decided (the Tenancy Officer)
questions.text: What did the participant decide about each support?
questions.hint: Write it in their words, with their reasons if they give them. "Not decided" is an answer. Never press for a choice. A choice can change at any time.

controls.label: One line each: support; chose us; chose another provider; chose none for now; not decided
Where they chose us: the date they asked and the date we gave our offer

questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 13, Procedure step 26.

questions.section: Section E: What the participant decided (the Tenancy Officer)
questions.text: When was the policy given?
questions.hint: Give the policy and the statement at least 3 before the participant is asked to sign the SDA service agreement. They may ask for less, in their own words. The days between this date and the signing date are checked at AGR-SDA-01 Q31 and PRO-SDA-04 step 15.

controls.label: If the participant asked for less than 3 business days: their own words

questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 13, Procedure step 26.

questions.section: Section E: What the participant decided (the Tenancy Officer)
questions.text: Did the participant raise a concern?
questions.hint: Start FRM-FBK-01 the same day and write its number here. Do not try to settle it yourself.

controls.label: If yes: the concern in their words

questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 13, Procedure step 26.

questions.section: Section E: What the participant decided (the Tenancy Officer)
questions.text: How did the participant acknowledge this record?
questions.hint: Not signing never changes their home or their supports.

options: chose not to sign, with the reason

questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 13, Procedure step 26.

questions.section: Section E: What the participant decided (the Tenancy Officer)
questions.text: When did the participant get a copy, and in what format?
questions.hint: Give the copy with the plain summary and the contacts.

controls.label: Format, Or the reason no copy was given

questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 14.

questions.section: Section F: Agreements and the offer (the SDA Manager)
questions.text: Are the agreements separate documents, and does any term link them?
questions.hint: The SDA service agreement is one document. Any support agreement from us is another, signed on its own. No term in either makes one depend on the other. Remove any linking term before signing.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 15. Recorded in: Register.

questions.section: Section F: Agreements and the offer (the SDA Manager)
questions.text: Was the offer of this place made with no condition about supports?
questions.hint: Check the offer, the agreement and anything said to the participant or their coordinator. We never ask which provider they will use. "No" means stop and tell the Chief Executive the same day.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 15, Procedure step 21. Recorded in: Register.

questions.section: Section G: Checks after a support change (the Tenancy Officer)
questions.text: What changed in the participant's supports, and when?
questions.hint: A new provider, a support ended, a support declined, or a concern raised.
questions.optional: Yes, only when Q3 is a support change
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 18.

questions.section: Section G: Checks after a support change (the Tenancy Officer)
questions.text: Since then, has anything about the participant's home changed?
questions.hint: Ask the participant in their usual way. Then check notices, rent, repairs, room, keys, visitors and how workers treat them.

controls.label: "Nothing has changed", or one line each: what

questions.optional: Yes, only when Q3 is a support change or the yearly review
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 18, Procedure step 26. Recorded in: Register.

questions.section: Section G: Checks after a support change (the Tenancy Officer)
questions.text: Has any provider the participant chose been refused, delayed, charged or put under a condition?
questions.hint: "Yes" starts step 20 of PRO-SDA-03.

controls.label: Date the provider was let in

questions.optional: Yes, only when Q3 is a support change or the yearly review
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 18, Procedure step 20, Procedure step 26.

questions.section: Section H: Before a tenancy action (the SDA Manager, then the Chief Executive)
questions.text: What tenancy action is planned, and on what legal ground?
questions.hint: A , a breach notice, any rent or board increase, a room move, or a change to the agreement or house rules for this participant. Give the ground in [state or territory tenancy law].
questions.optional: Yes, only when a tenancy action is planned
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 22. Recorded in: Register.

questions.section: Section H: Before a tenancy action (the SDA Manager, then the Chief Executive)
questions.text: In the last 12 months, has the participant changed, ended or declined a support, or raised a concern?
questions.hint: Use the REG-GOV-02 disclosure entries and REG-FBK-01. "Yes" does not stop the action. It makes the check at Q35 matter.
questions.optional: Yes, only when a tenancy action is planned
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 22.

questions.section: Section H: Before a tenancy action (the SDA Manager, then the Chief Executive)
questions.text: Does anything link the action to the participant's support decisions or concerns?
questions.hint: Use Decision table 4 in PRO-SDA-03. Look at the timing, who asked for the action, the evidence for the ground, and whether we would take the same action for another resident.

options: no link, the ground stands alone

questions.optional: Yes, only when a tenancy action is planned
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 23. Recorded in: Register.

questions.section: Section H: Before a tenancy action (the SDA Manager, then the Chief Executive)
questions.text: Who checked, and what did they decide?
questions.hint: The Chief Executive, or [independent contact for concerns] when the Chief Executive or a sole trader has an interest in the participant's supports. Never the person who plans the action.
questions.optional: Yes, only when a tenancy action is planned
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 23. Recorded in: Register.

questions.section: Section I: Review and links (the SDA Manager)
questions.text: When is the next review?
questions.hint: No more than 12 months from today. Sooner when anything in Section C changes.
questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 16, Procedure step 26.

questions.section: Section I: Review and links (the SDA Manager)
questions.text: Which other records are linked?
questions.hint: Complaints, incidents, risks and declarations from FRM-GOV-01, each with its register number. Write "none" if there are none.

controls.label: Register and number, one line each

questions.trail: Asked at: Procedure step 16.

form.intro:
Use this record to show that we told a participant in a specialist disability accommodation (SDA) dwelling three things. First, what interests we hold. Second, that their home and their supports are separate. Third, that their home does not depend on the supports they choose.

Complete one record each time one of these happens:

  • we offer a place in an SDA dwelling, before the participant signs anything
  • we offer a support from us or a related business, or the participant asks about one
  • our interests change: a new support, a new related business, a new owner or a new landlord
  • the participant changes, ends or declines a support or a provider
  • a is planned for the participant
  • 12 months have passed since the last record, even when nothing has changed
  • an interest of ours ends.

Who completes it: the completes Sections A, B, D, E and G with the participant. The completes Sections C, F and I, and Q33 and Q34 in Section H. The Chief Executive completes Q35 and Q36. When a tenancy action is planned, only Sections A, H and I are completed: no participant meeting is held and no participant signature is sought. The participant never has to fill in a form to be heard.

When | Complete these questions:

  • Before the participant signs the ; we offer or they ask about a support; our interests changed; an interest ended | Sections A to F (Q1 to Q29), then Section I
  • The participant changed, ended or declined a support or a provider | Sections A, G and I (Q1 to Q4, Q30 to Q32, Q37 and Q38); Sections D and E only where our interests also changed
  • A tenancy action is planned | Sections A, H and I only (Q1 to Q4, Q33 to Q38); no participant meeting, no participant signature
  • Yearly review, or the participant asks for a review | Sections A, B, D, E, G and I (Q1 to Q7, Q13 to Q27, Q31, Q32, Q37 and Q38)
  • A concern was raised | Sections A, E (Q25) and I

Have ready:

  • the participant's FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form
  • the open rows of REG-GOV-02 Conflict of Interest Register for this dwelling
  • STA-GOV-01 Conflict of Interest: Plain Summary, in the participant's format
  • the SDA agreement and any support agreement, as separate documents
  • the contacts for an advocate, a tenancy advice service and the NDIS Commission.

What happens next: the SDA Manager enters it in REG-GOV-02 within 2 business days. PRO-SDA-03 Conflict of Interest Procedure (Specialist Disability Accommodation) sets every step.

This record never ends a tenancy and authorises no tenancy action. A participant can say no to every support we offer and keep their home.
form.privacy:
We collect this information to show that the participant understood our interests and that their choices were their own. We also collect it to meet the NDIS Practice Standards and the NDIS Code of Conduct.

The Tenancy Officer, the SDA Manager and the Chief Executive read it. When a tenancy action is planned, the person who checks it reads it too. In REG-GOV-02 we write the participant's number, never their name. We write no other resident's name on this record. An auditor or the NDIS Commission may see it as the law allows.

The participant can see this record and ask us to correct it. They use FRM-INF-02 Request to Access or Correct Personal Information Form, or they ask any worker. Asking never puts their home at risk. We tell the participant's other providers only what the participant agrees we may tell them. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect this record.
form.after:
• Tenancy Officer: give the completed record to the SDA Manager within 1 business day of the meeting (our standard).
  • SDA Manager: enter the record in REG-GOV-02 within 2 business days of the meeting (our standard).
  • SDA Manager: read Section G within 2 business days of receiving it. If a provider was refused, start step 20 of PRO-SDA-03 the same day. If the participant links a change to their support choice, start step 25 the same day (our standard).
  • SDA Manager: send Section H to the Chief Executive before the tenancy action goes out. The Chief Executive completes Q35 and Q36 within 1 business day of receiving it (our standard).
  • If the Chief Executive or a sole trader has an interest in the participant's supports, give Section H to [independent contact for concerns].
  • Tenancy Officer: give the participant their copy within 2 business days of the meeting (our standard).
  • SDA Manager: set the review date at Q37. Start a new record on that date.
  • The signed record is filed on the participant's file and kept for 7 years after the REG-GOV-02 row is closed (NDIS Act 2013, section 45B, from 27 August 2026: records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years).

register.proves:
This register is the one running record of how [Provider name] manages each tenancy in its specialist disability accommodation (SDA) . Each row is one record. It shows what was done, who took part, what the said and chose, and who checked.

It holds nine kinds of record: tenancy, arrangement, vacancy, notice rule, notice, change, home event, concern and review. An arrangement is the agreement with the participant's providers. A concern is anything raised about a dwelling that is not yet a complaint, a repair or an incident.

Complaints, incidents and repairs are not copied here. They stay in REG-FBK-01 Complaints Register, REG-INC-01 Incident Register and REG-SDA-01 SDA Dwelling Register. A row here links to them in column O.

In this register:

  • "SDA Conditions Rule" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation Conditions) Rule 2018.
  • "SDA Rules 2020" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Specialist Disability Accommodation) Rules 2020.
  • "Incident Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018.
  • "Complaints Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Complaints Management and Resolution) Rules 2018.
  • "Restrictive Practices Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.
  • "" means the Service Manager for our SDA dwellings. "" means the worker the SDA Manager assigns tenancy tasks to; in a small provider this is the SDA Manager. "" means a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.
  • Indicators evidenced: s 72 (1) to (5), (8) and (9), including s 72 (3)(a) to (3)(h). Columns O and BL link to the complaints and incident records that evidence s 72 (6) and (7); those indicators are proved by the complaints and incident systems, not here. A SIL provider that signs an arrangement can use its arrangement row for Module 5A, sections 72A to 72E (from 1 July 2026).
  • Legal basis: NDIS Act 2013, section 73F(2)(a) and (c). It makes compliance with the law and the NDIS Practice Standards a condition of registration. The SDA Conditions Rule (sections 6 and 8 to 11) and the SDA Rules 2020 (sections 24, 29 and 32) set duties; section 37 of the SDA Rules 2020 is the equivalent of Conditions Rule section 10(2)(b) for registered providers of supports. This register evidences them. No NDIS rule sets the columns. They are our standard, built from the indicators and those duties.
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years from the day it is closed or superseded (our standard). NDIS Act 2013, section 45B (from 27 August 2026): records of claims and supports are kept for 7 years, so 7 years is also the statutory floor. An incident or complaint record has its own limit. It is 7 years from the day it is made (statutory: Incident Rules, section 12(4); Complaints Rules, section 10(3)).
  • Other law can require longer, for example about bonds. Check the law of [state or territory] before any row is destroyed.

Which columns apply:

  • Every row fills columns A to O. These are the spine.
  • A tenancy row also fills columns P to W.
  • An arrangement row also fills columns X to AH. Every tenancy has an arrangement row. Where no SIL provider delivers supports in the dwelling to the participant, the row says so and sets a date to check again.
  • A vacancy row also fills columns AI to AT.
  • A notice rule row fills columns AU and AV.
  • A notice row also fills columns AW to BE.
  • A change row also fills columns BF to BH.
  • A home event row also fills columns BI to BN.
  • A review row also fills column BO.
  • A concern row also fills columns BP to BS.
register.entry:
1. The SDA Manager owns the register and approves the closing of every row. The Tenancy Officer adds tenancy, arrangement, vacancy, change and concern rows. The SDA Manager adds notice rows, notice rule rows, home event rows and monthly review rows. The Tenancy Officer completes the service and review rights columns of a notice row, and opens a notice row for a participant's own notice. The Quality Manager adds the 3-monthly and 12-monthly review rows.
  2. Add a row within 2 business days of the event (our standard). Five rows are faster. Open a vacancy row within 1 business day of learning of the vacancy. Open a home event row within 1 business day. Open a concern row within 1 business day, when the concern is acknowledged. Open a notice rule row before the first notice of that kind. Enter a notice row before the notice is served.
  3. Use one row for each event. Where a record concerns several residents, columns AM, AO and AP hold one dated line for each person.
  4. Name participants by participant number. Name applicants by applicant number only. Never write an applicant's name in this register.
  5. Keep health details, diagnoses and behaviour support plan content out of the register. Put them on the participant's own file and give the file reference in column N.
  6. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason.
  7. A new SIL provider, or a change to who is responsible for a matter, is a new arrangement row. Set the old row to "superseded" on the same day.
  8. Nobody enters or approves a row about their own decision. The second approver in column AX is never the person who decided.
  9. When systems are down, write the record on paper. Enter the row within 2 business days of the system coming back.

A row is closed only when all of these are true:

  • every column required for its record type is filled
  • each action in column J is done, or sits in REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register with an owner and a due date
  • the participant was told the outcome, and column K shows the date and way
  • the SDA Manager has approved closing.

A tenancy row stays "current" until column W is filled. An arrangement row stays "current" until a new row supersedes it. A vacancy row closes when column AT is filled, or when the SDA Manager records that the place is withdrawn. A notice rule row stays "current" until the law changes and a new row supersedes it. A notice row closes when column BE shows the result. A change row closes when column BG or column BH is filled and the participant was told. A home event row closes when the action in column BM is done, or is tracked in REG-QMS-01. A concern row closes when column BR is filled and column BS shows where it went and how the person was told.
